Why it matters: Keeps attribution intact from first call to closing so contracts and fees count for the right channel.

Type: Lookup to Campaign (copied from lead, locked)
Required when: Copied when the deal is created; not editable after
Why it matters: Contracts per campaign and ROI by campaign both read this field.

Required when: Always
Why it matters: Separates deals that are booked from deals that are actually kept.

Required when: Before Deal Status can move to Offer Sent
Why it matters: After-repair value from comps. Everything in MAO starts here.

Required when: Before Deal Status can move to Offer Sent
Why it matters: Your team's repair number, the one MAO uses.

Required when: When a buyer walks the property (optional)
Why it matters: What the end buyer thinks repairs cost. Comparing it with yours shows whether your estimates run low.

Required when: Calculated: Buyer's Repair Estimate − Your Repair Estimate
Why it matters: A gap that keeps growing in one direction means your offers are built on the wrong repair numbers.

Required when: Before Deal Status can move to Offer Sent
Why it matters: The rule percentage, stored on the deal so every rep uses the same one.

Required when: Before Deal Status can move to Offer Sent
Why it matters: The target fee you plan to earn, built into MAO instead of hoped for later.

Required when: Calculated: ARV × MAO % − Your Repair Estimate − Assignment Fee
Why it matters: One maximum allowable offer per deal, calculated the same way for everyone.

Required when: Before Deal Status can move to Offer Sent
Why it matters: The number actually offered to the seller.

Required when: Calculated: TRUE when Offer Amount > MAO
Why it matters: Flags offers that need a second look before they go out (see automation-rules.md).

Required when: When Offer Above MAO is TRUE, before Offer Sent
Why it matters: Records that someone other than the rep signed off on an above-MAO offer.

Required when: Stamped when Deal Status changes to Under Contract
Why it matters: Start of the clock for days to assign and for contract to first seller call.

Required when: Stamped by the first logged call to the seller after Contract Signed Date
Why it matters: Shows whether anyone kept the seller warm after signing.

Field name: Hours Contract to First Seller Call
Required when: Calculated: (First Seller Call After Contract − Contract Signed Date) in hours
Why it matters: One of the Monday 5. Long silences after signing are where cancellations start.

Required when: When Deal Status changes to Assigned
Why it matters: The day an end buyer signed the assignment.

Required when: Calculated: Assigned Date − Contract Signed Date
Why it matters: How long dispo takes. Slow assignment eats into inspection periods and raises fall-out risk.

Required when: When Deal Status changes to Closed
Why it matters: The day the fee was actually paid.

Required when: When Deal Status changes to Under Contract; locked after
Why it matters: The fee you expected at signing. This is the forecast.

Required when: When Deal Status changes to Closed (0 if Fell Out)
Why it matters: The fee actually received. ROI should be counted on this, not on Booked Fee.

Required when: When you keep the property (for example as a rental) instead of assigning it
Why it matters: Deals you keep still came from a campaign. Leaving them out undercounts that campaign's ROI.

Picklist values: Seller backed out; Title issue; No buyer found; Buyer backed out; Inspection or repairs; Renegotiated; Other
Required when: When Deal Status = Fell Out, or when Kept Fee is lower than Booked Fee
Why it matters: Tells you whether fall-outs come from underwriting, dispo or the seller relationship.
